I am an old man now, sixty years, and I have been farming these lands in the North West all my life. This beans plot, half a hectare plus small, I intercrop as my fathers did — beans with small guinea corn between, so the soil stays strong and if one fails the other feeds us. I will put a little NPK at planting because the land is tired, and spread the manure from my goats and cattle that I gathered in the dry season. I cannot afford to irrigate or buy the expensive hybrid seed from town — I keep my own seed from last harvest, and I spray small insecticide when the pod-borers come, otherwise the weevils finish everything. My sons and their wives will weed with me, but at harvest I must hire some youth from the village because my back is not what it was.
